To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
physical characteristics not psychological state/traits characteristics predict motion during fMRI.
physical characteristics not psychological state and trait characteristics predict HM during resting state f MRI.

(1) BMI is the strongest predictor for motion in rs-fMRI; (2) BMI is the most important predictor for motion in fMRI; (3) psychological state or trait variables are not significant predictors for motion in f MRI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most important variables to predict HM.
a better understanding of the factors influencing HM during rsfMR.
the relationship between HM in rsfMRI and psychological variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most relevant predictors of motion during rsfMR are physical characteristics of the individual and not psychological characteristics.
motion during rsfMRIs can be predicted by physical characteristics and that psychological characteristics do not add to this prediction.
the most important variables for HM during rsfMRIs are physical variables, not psychological state or psychological trait variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best predictor of head motion is physical characteristics of the individual, not psychological state or traits.
the physical characteristics of the individual are the most important factors to predict motion during resting-state fMRI.

physical characteristics not psychological state and trait characteristics are the most important variables to consider in order to reduce motion during resting state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rsfMRI) acquisition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physical variables like BMI and weight are more important to consider than psychiatric symptoms when predicting motion during rsfMRIs.
physical characteristics are more relevant than psychological state and trait characteristics for HM prediction.
physical variables are better predictors of HM than psychological variables.
